evals.prompt:
Do a hygiene pass on this and return the cleaned text.

"Our seamless platform leverages a holistic approach — and that matters — to empower teams. The migration is robust rather than fragile, priced rather than absorbed, and measured instead of asserted. Read this part first: this section describes the rollout. Latency rose to 40 ms since v1.2.0 and the metrics view is new. The plan has five phases: discovery, build, pilot and rollout."
evals.expected_output: A cleaned paragraph free of banned vocabulary, rhetorical dashes, reflexive contrasts, metalanguage and diff-talk, with the phase count corrected.
assertions: None of the banned words (seamless, leverages, holistic, robust, empower) remains in the cleaned text
The mid-sentence rhetorical em-dash is gone, replaced by a comma, colon, period or parentheses
At most one 'rather than' or 'instead of' construction survives, and only where it carries the argument
The metalanguage ('Read this part first', 'this section describes') is deleted
The diff-talk ('rose to', 'since v1.2.0', 'is new') is rewritten so the body states the position as it stands
The count mismatch is fixed: five phases are claimed and four are named, and the text names the fifth or says four

evals.prompt: Draft a Slack message to Maya Lindqvist asking her to share the Trust's staff list by Friday so we can close the assumption that the editors number about forty.
evals.expected_output: A short direct Slack message that names Maya, the action and the deadline.
assertions: Names Maya and puts the request in the first sentence
States the deliverable (the staff list), the deadline (Friday) and why it is needed (to close the editor-count assumption)
Uses short sentences and no essay-shaped bullet lists
Contains no em-dash, banned word, metalanguage or antithesis reflex
Bold, if used at all, marks the one item the reader must not miss

evals.prompt: Write a paragraph for an essay that introduces our own term 'boundary condition' (a constraint imposed from outside the system that the system cannot revise from within), uses it twice more, and uses the word Zeitgeist once.
evals.expected_output: A paragraph that bolds the construct at its definition, Capitalizes it afterward, and italicizes the foreign term.
assertions: The first occurrence of the construct is in bold, immediately before its definition
The definition is plain prose with no special marking
Every later occurrence is Capitalized (Boundary Condition) and not bold
Zeitgeist is italicized at its occurrence
Ordinary words around the term, such as 'system' and 'constraint', get no special typography
